parameterNotes.service: the service whose mapper threw; the failure share is a share of that service's responses, so the name is the subject rather than a reading.
parameterNotes.endpoint: the route the guard sits behind, which is how the ticket separates this route from the ones that stayed clean; no series here is per route.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: The response mapper fills the subscription field only for an account with an active subscription, and it writes the key either way: for an account created after the migration the key is present and holds null rather than being absent. The guard in the summary handler tests for absence, so a null passes it and the next statement dereferences it, which throws inside the handler for /v2/summary and for no other route. Nothing about the request is unusual and no account is expired; the difference is when the account was created, which is why the failures read as a share of traffic rather than as an outage. The migration is the trigger and not the defect: it changed what the mapper writes, and the guard had been asking the wrong question since it was written. A guard that accepts either a missing key or a null one reproduces every response the endpoint used to produce, which is the repair the case states rather than an opinion about one.

rootCauseIndicators.description: the share of /v2/summary responses that failed, which is a property of one endpoint and not of the service
the share of mapped accounts whose field is present and null, which is the population the guard lets through
the exception's own frame, which names the line that dereferences and nothing about the caller

causalChain.mechanism: the summary handler dereferences a field the mapper wrote as null, so the request throws inside the pod and every other route the pod serves keeps answering

callers of /v2/summary receive a 500 for the accounts whose field is null and a normal response for every other account, so the service sees a share of failures on one route while its health and its other routes stay green

evidenceCheckpoints.description: the failed share of one endpoint, which is what a caller sees: not an outage, because eleven of twelve requests still succeed
the share of mapped accounts whose field is present and null, which is the set the guard was supposed to refuse and did not
the exception's frame, which is the only reading that names the line: the failure is a dereference rather than a schema change or a timeout, and the line it names is the same one every time

remediation.action: treat a present-and-null field as the absent case in the guard, so the response carries the default the mapper means rather than a dereference of it
assert the mapper's output shape in the export step rather than only the mapper's input, because the migration that triggered this changed what was written and not what was read

query: The reporting service began returning 500 on /v2/summary alone, with a stack trace that ends on one line every time. Which component holds the defect, and what about the account decides whether a request fails?
